ants.description: ANTs extracts information from complex datasets that include imaging. Paired with ANTsR, ANTs is useful for managing, interpreting and visualizing multidimensional data. ANTs is popularly considered a state-of-the-art medical image registration and segmentation toolkit. ANTsR is an emerging tool supporting standardized multimodality image analysis. ANTs depends on the Insight ToolKit (ITK), a widely used medical image processing library to which ANTs developers contribute. A summary of some ANTs findings and tutorial material (most of which is on this page) is here.\

cryosparc.description: CryoSPARC (Structura Biotechnology) is a GPU-accelerated platform for single-particle cryo-EM: motion and CTF correction, particle picking, 2D classification, ab-initio reconstruction and refinement, run through a browser-based interface. https://cryosparc.com **This container does not include CryoSPARC.** CryoSPARC needs a licence ID (free for non-profit academic research, commercial licence otherwise), and its licence forbids redistributing the software. The container provides the Ubuntu 24.04 runtime and tools that CryoSPARC's installer and services need, plus the `cryosparc` launcher. The launcher downloads CryoSPARC with your own licence ID into a directory you can write to and runs it from there. The container version 1.0.0 is the launcher version, not a CryoSPARC version. You choose the CryoSPARC release at install time; the default is the latest release. ### Install once 1. Request a licence ID: https://cryosparc.com/download 2. Pick a writable directory with several GB free that keeps the same path in future sessions (not inside the container image). Run the container with GPU access (`apptainer exec --nv`), then:

ctffind.description: CTFFIND estimates the defocus, astigmatism and optional phase shift of electron micrographs by fitting the contrast transfer function (CTF) to their amplitude spectra. This container builds CTFFIND 4.1.14 from the official source release with FFTW and OpenMP threading. It runs on the CPU and needs no GPU. CTFFIND 4.1.14 is the release that RELION drives through its "Use CTFFIND-4.1?" option. CTFFIND 5 adds an extra "Determine sample thickness?" prompt that RELION does not answer, so RELION jobs stop at the expert-options prompt. Run `ctffind` and answer the prompts, or script them from standard input:

elastix.description: a toolbox for rigid and nonrigid registration of images. elastix is open source software, based on the well-known Insight Segmentation and Registration Toolkit (ITK). The software consists of a collection of algorithms that are commonly used to perform (medical) image registration: the task of finding a spatial transformation, mapping one image (the fixed image) to another (the moving image), by optimizing relevant image similarity metrics. The modular design of elastix allows the user to quickly configure, test, and compare different registration methods for a specific application. A command-line interface enables automated processing of large numbers of data sets, by means of scripting. Nowadays elastix is accompanied by ITKElastix making it available in Python (on Pypi) and by SimpleElastix, making it available in languages like C++, Python, Java, R, Ruby, C# and Lua.
elastix.citation:

motioncor3.description: MotionCor3 corrects beam-induced motion in cryo-EM and cryo-ET movies on NVIDIA GPUs. It is the open-source (BSD-3-Clause) successor of UCSF MotionCor2. It reads MRC, TIFF and EER movies. It performs whole-frame and local patch alignment, dose weighting and gain/defect correction, and estimates CTF. This container builds MotionCor3 1.2.4 (commit dd8b6831ae66ef016fb7ef3b9b6172f8b56c79aa) from source with CUDA 12.8. It contains native kernels for compute capability 7.0 to 12.0 (Volta to Blackwell) and PTX for newer GPUs. MotionCor2 is not included: its UCSF licence forbids redistribution without written permission. MotionCor3 is an improved implementation of MotionCor2 and keeps its option names (-InMrc, -OutMrc, -Patch, ...). Requirements: - An NVIDIA GPU with a CUDA 12 capable driver (525 or newer). The driver library (libcuda.so.1) comes from the host, so run the container with GPU support, for example `apptainer exec --nv`. - Without a GPU only `MotionCor3 --help` style inspection is possible; alignment needs a GPU.
motioncor3.citation: Zheng SQ, Palovcak E, Armache JP, Verba KA, Cheng Y, Agard DA. MotionCor2: anisotropic correction of beam-induced motion for improved cryo-electron microscopy. Nature Methods 14, 331-332 (2017). doi:10.1038/nmeth.4193

nextpyp.description: nextPYP (Bartesaghi lab, Duke University) is a web application for single-particle cryo-EM and cryo-electron tomography: pre-processing, particle picking, sub-tomogram averaging, constrained refinement and classification, run as projects in a browser. https://nextpyp.app nextPYP runs as two Apptainer images. This container includes the web server image (`nextPYP.sif`) and the `nextpyp` launcher. The processing image (`pyp.sif`, about 43 GB) is too large to include, so `nextpyp install` downloads it once into a directory you choose. The web server then runs from that directory in a nested Apptainer container. ### Install once Pick a writable directory with at least 50 GB free plus room for your projects (raw movies and tilt series need several TB). Every parent directory must be group- and world-executable (`chmod go+x`), which nextPYP enforces, so use project or scratch storage rather than a private home directory.

niimath.description: It is said that `imitation is the sincerest form of flattery`. This project emulates the popular [fslmaths](https://fsl.fmrib.ox.ac.uk/fslcourse/lectures/practicals/intro3/index.html) tool. fslmaths is advertised as a `general image calculator` and is not only one of the foundational tools for FSL's brain imaging pipelines (such as [FEAT](https://fsl.fmrib.ox.ac.uk/fsl/fslwiki/FEAT)), but has also been widely adopted by many tools. This popularity suggests that it fulfills an important niche. While scientists are often encouraged to discover novel solutions, it sometimes seems that replication is undervalued. No writable home directory is required. Set NUMBA_CACHE_DIR or MPLCONFIGDIR to your own writable paths to retain caches. Mount your metadata, images and output directory at runtime. relion.description: RELION (REgularised LIkelihood OptimisatioN) is a stand-alone program for Maximum A Posteriori refinement of 3D reconstructions and 2D class averages in cryo-electron microscopy. This container builds RELION 5.1.1 from source for CUDA compute capabilities 7.0, 7.5, 8.0, 8.6, 8.9 and 9.0, with PTX for newer GPUs, and includes helper integrations for CTFFIND and MotionCor2. A bundled Python environment with CUDA PyTorch 2.7.1+cu128 provides the RELION Python programs: Blush regularisation, the 2D class ranker, DynaMight, Topaz, ModelAngelo, the tomography tools and the amyloid tracer. The Blush and class ranker model weights are installed in `TORCH_HOME=/opt/relion-5.1.1/torch`. ModelAngelo and the amyloid tracer download their model weights on first use, which needs a writable `TORCH_HOME`, for example `export TORCH_HOME=~/.cache/torch`. Blush and the class ranker then download their weights there too.
relion.citation: Sjors H W Scheres. RELION: Implementation of a Bayesian approach to cryo-EM structure determination. Journal of Structural Biology, 180(3):519-530, December 2012. doi:10.1016/j.jsb.2012.09.006.

scipion.description: Scipion is an image processing framework for cryo-electron microscopy. It integrates many cryo-EM packages into reproducible, traceable workflows that you build and run from a graphical project manager or from Python. This container installs Scipion 3.9.0 with scipion-installer 3.0.0 into a conda environment (Python 3.10.22) under /opt/scipion: - scipion-app 3.9.0 - scipion-pyworkflow 3.12.0 - scipion-em (pwem) 3.11.1 Run `scipion3` to open the project manager (Tk GUI). Other useful commands: - `scipion3 version` prints the installed package versions - `scipion3 protocols` lists the available protocols - `scipion3 printenv` shows the effective configuration - `scipion3 python script.py` runs a script with pyworkflow and pwem importable - `scipion3 tests --help` lists the built-in test runner options Projects are stored in `SCIPION_USER_DATA`, which defaults to `~/ScipionUserData`. If your home directory is not writable, the launcher falls back to `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ScipionUserData-<uid>` and prints a warning. Set `SCIPION_USER_DATA` to a persistent directory to keep projects in that case. Test datasets downloaded by `scipion3 testdata` go to `$SCIPION_USER_DATA/data/tests` unless `SCIPION_TESTS` is set. A personal configuration file at `~/.config/scipion/scipion.conf`, or the file named by `SCIPION_LOCAL_CONFIG`, overrides the defaults. The container provides the Scipion core and the protocols bundled with pwem (data import, subsets, masks and others). It does not include plugins that wrap external programs (Xmipp, RELION, CTFFIND, MotionCor2, ...). The installation is read-only, so `scipion3 installp` and the plugin manager cannot add plugins at runtime. Use the dedicated Neurodesk containers for those programs. Documentation: https://scipion-em.github.io/docs/

integration, reproducibility and validation in 3D electron microscopy.

This software called Shape AnaLysis Toolbox (SALT), will enhance the intuitiveness and ease of use for such studies, as well as allow researchers to find shape changes with higher statistical power. Altogether this constitutes a crucial resource for the imaging field that will enable many and important new findings in biomedical imaging studies.

smartscope.description: SmartScope (NIEHS and Duke University) screens cryo-EM grids automatically. It drives the microscope through SerialEM: it acquires an atlas, finds and ranks squares and holes, collects high-magnification images and reports CTF and ice-thickness estimates in a web interface. https://smartscope.org Upstream ships SmartScope as several docker-compose services. This container runs them all from one image: MariaDB, Redis, the SmartScope web application (gunicorn behind nginx) and its Celery worker. It also includes IMOD 5.1.13 (`alignframes`) and CTFFIND 5.0.2, which SmartScope uses to process high-magnification movies. ### Create an instance once An instance directory holds the database, settings, logs and screening data. Choose a writable directory that keeps the same path in later sessions. The container image itself is read-only.

xmipp.description: Xmipp is a suite of image processing programs for cryo-electron microscopy: micrograph and particle handling, CTF estimation, 2D classification, 3D reconstruction, volume analysis and metadata utilities. https://github.com/I2PC/xmipp This container builds Xmipp 6.0.0 standalone, not as a Scipion plugin, with xmippCore 4.1.0 and xmippViz 4.0.2. It is a CPU build with OpenMPI support. CUDA programs are not included. All `xmipp_*` programs are installed in /opt/xmipp/bin, for example: xmipp_phantom_create -i phantom.descr -o phantom.mrc xmipp_image_header -i phantom.mrc xmipp_image_statistics -i phantom.mrc MPI programs (`xmipp_mpi_*`) run with `mpirun -np N`. The Python binding `xmippLib` (pyxmipp3 0.4.0) is on PYTHONPATH. The Java viewer `xmipp_showj` needs a graphical desktop. Deep-learning programs that need Xmipp's separate conda environments are not set up, and some Python scripts need extra packages (for example PyWavelets) that are not installed. The build runs CMake directly with the options of upstream's `./xmipp` installer. Every source, including those CMake would clone from moving branches, comes from a pinned, checksummed archive.
